takeaway: Marple combines compressed spike templates with a streaming accelerator, projecting real-time sorting of 10,000 neural channels at 78.94 mW in a scaled 7 nm design.
background: Spike sorting maps recorded electrical spikes to individual neurons. High-density probes now stream thousands of channels, but wearable brain-machine interfaces face tight power, area, and thermal budgets.
villain: Software sorters need desktop-class compute and offline processing, while prior hardware handles far fewer channels; template storage becomes the dominant memory cost at scale.
approach: Marple's fixed-function front end filters and whitens serialized samples, detects neighborhood peaks, and emits 60-sample windows from nine nearby channels. Its vector back end compares those windows with offline-generated templates compressed by centroid differences, quantization, segmented delta encoding, duplicate removal, and trimmed numeric fields. Decompression occurs on demand, so the design assumes prerecorded templates and the paper's channel-neighborhood, sampling-rate, and peak-rate model.
impact: The authors argue that this co-design makes contemporary template matching plausible for much larger untethered neural interfaces than prior hardware sorters.

evaluation.overview: The paper combines analytical scaling, compression experiments on SpikeForest and synthetic MEArec Neuropixels recordings, and RTL synthesis and place-and-route estimates; it does not report fabricated silicon or an in-vivo deployment.
evaluation.implemented: A Verilog pipeline covering filtering, whitening, peak detection, buffering, template decompression, and vector template matching, synthesized and laid out in a commercial 65 nm flow with SRAM modeled by CACTI.
evaluation.setting: The target configuration has 10,000 channels, 30,000 neurons, 30 kHz sampling, 300 MHz operation, up to 20 spikes/s/neuron, and 13 templates/channel; compression used 87 SpikeForest recordings plus twenty 384-channel, 1,500-neuron MEArec recordings combined into larger synthetic sets.
baselines: Uncompressed FP32 template representation and matching
Commodity CPU and GPU estimates for the modeled pipeline

results.text: The authors report 8–11× template-storage reduction while retaining more than 99% relative matching accuracy.
For the modeled 10,000-channel, 30,000-neuron configuration, scaling the 65 nm post-layout design to 7 nm yielded projected totals of 78.94 mW and 4.25 mm².

limitations: Power and area are projections from a 65 nm post-layout model scaled to 7 nm, not measurements from fabricated silicon or an untethered implant. The real-time path assumes offline-generated templates, high-scale accuracy is evaluated on synthetic MEArec recordings, and the explored CNN replacement does not meet the large-scale real-time budget.
phd_group_signal: The work links an application-level scaling model to compression design, streaming microarchitecture, RTL implementation, physical-design estimates, and a clearly separated exploratory CNN alternative.

claims.text: Marple uses a fixed streaming front end to produce 60-sample windows over nine-channel neighborhoods, then decompresses offline-generated templates on demand for vector template matching.
The target model assumes 10,000 channels sampled at 30 kHz, 30,000 neurons, a peak firing rate of 20 spikes/s/neuron, and at most 13 templates per channel.

Large-scale recordings are synthesized with MEArec, and the reported 7 nm power and area are projections obtained by scaling a commercial 65 nm post-layout design rather than measurements from fabricated silicon.
Compression experiments used 87 SpikeForest recordings and twenty 384-channel, 1,500-neuron MEArec recordings, with the synthetic recordings combined to model up to 30,000 neurons.

sources.title: Marple: Scalable Spike Sorting for Untethered Brain-Machine Interfacing
supports: Full paper abstract, introduction, background, compression method, accelerator design, evaluation, assumptions, limitations, and conclusion.

notes: Read the abstract; Sections 1, 2, 3.1-3.2, 4, 5, and 7; and Figures 4-12 and Tables 3-8 needed for the workload model, mechanism, evidence boundary, and results.

The abstract reports 78.08 mW, while the detailed Section 5.2 text and Table 7 report 78.94 mW; the summary uses the detailed result and preserves this source inconsistency as unresolved.
